title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1986 'algèbre des figures'. A figure F in an ambient set L is a finite stratified set. It is given by a surjection φ: S → I, with S ⊂ L and I a finite ordered set. The pieces are A_i = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}), with open strata A_i°, and the support is |F| = S. There are three relations on the set 𝓕 of figures:
- F ≤ G: F is a sub-figure of G.
- F ≼ G: F is a subdivision of G, so |F| = |G| and the stratification R_F is finer.
- F ≪ G: F refines G.

The Proposition on p.25 says F ≪ G ⇔ ∃G' with F ≤ G' ≼ G. In words, a refinement is a sub-figure of a subdivision. The 'if' part constructs G' by adjoining singleton pieces {x} for x ∈ |G| \ |F|.

This page opens with the consequence: ≪ is the composite of ≤ and ≼, and conversely ≼ is ≪ restricted to equal supports. So ≪ and ≼ determine each other 'in terms of ≤'. Grothendieck then asks (marked '??') whether ≤ can conversely be expressed through ≪ and ≼. This question is left open.

NB. In the concrete setting, F ≤ G and F ≼ G together imply F = G, since a sub-figure with full support is everything. He wants this to hold in an abstract 'contexte' (an axiomatised class of admissible figures, with axioms C1–C8…).
- Proposed axiom: if F ≤ G and F ≠ G, there is a nonempty H, disjoint from F, with H ≪ G. This is the complementary pieces.
- Then if also F ≼ G, axiom C5 makes H disjoint from G. That contradicts the lemma: H ≪ G and H disjoint from G imply H = ∅.
- Proof of the lemma: write H ≤ G' ≼ G. By C5 (and C8), H is disjoint from G'. A sub-figure disjoint from its ambient figure is empty.

Finally he checks the context axioms:
- C5 (if F ≼ G, then H is disjoint from F iff disjoint from G) is clear, because |F| = |G| and disjointness of figures is read off supports, |H| ∩ |H'| = ∅.
- C6 (subdivision…) is deferred: 'on le verra tantôt'.
- C7 (extension of a subdivision) is OK modulo topological verifications.
- C8 is trivial.

The purpose is to axiomatise a 'context' of figures (PL, semi-algebraic, tame…). The goal is to recover the order-theoretic structure (sub-figure, subdivision, refinement) from a minimal set of axioms.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is a small, correct order-theoretic lemma.
The opening '??' question (express ≤ via ≪ and ≼) is not answered on this page. Only the partial fact (≤ ∩ ≼ = equality) is established.

ideas.what: Refinement = sub-figure of a subdivision, so ≪ = ≤ ∘ ≼, and the relations determine each other
ideas.modern_name: subcomplex of a subdivision; refinement of stratifications/cell complexes

ideas.what: Lemma: F ≤ G and F ≼ G imply F = G, proved axiomatically from a 'complement' axiom plus C5
ideas.modern_name: antisymmetry/compatibility of subobject and subdivision orders

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'contextes' (axioms C5–C8) for admissible figures: disjointness detected by supports, extension of subdivisions
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimality), Shiota; Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology programmatically, not these axioms

missed.claim: Open question whether the sub-figure order ≤ is definable from the refinement order ≪ and the subdivision order ≼ alone. This is a purely order-theoretic reconstruction question for a tame 'context'.
missed.quote: Peut-on de même exprimer ≤ en termes de ≪ et de ≼?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It bears on whether a category of tame stratified spaces can be presented by refinement data alone (cf. exit-path / stratified-space frameworks). It is likely easy to settle.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine order-theoretic checks within Grothendieck's axiomatisation of 'figures'. The only interest is the unpublished axiomatic 'contexte' framework itself and a small open definability question.
transcription_corrections: The symbol rendered \precneqq is the subdivision relation ≼ (curly ≤, same as on p.25), not a strict relation.
'Qu'en est-il des contours énoncés des contextes' should probably read 'Qu'en est-il des conditions énoncées des contextes'.
In the C5 line, 'tels que, on |F|=|G|' is likely 'trivial, car |F|=|G| et disjonction de H avec H' se voit par les supports par |H|∩|H'|=∅'.
'donc absurde [?]' may read 'donc on conviendrait; ceci…'. The image is ambiguous.
C7: 'OK – la vérification topologique' (verification of the topological condition).
